keyVerseText: And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
rootMeaning: The word στιγμή (stigmḗ) is the feminine form of στίγμα (stígma), which means 'mark' or 'brand'—a mark incised or punched to indicate ownership or identity. This root meaning conveys the idea of a precise, pointed mark, which metaphorically extends to a very brief, pinpointed moment in time. Thus, στιγμή carries the sense of a sharply defined instant, much like a puncture or spot that is distinct and unmistakable, adding a vividness to the common English gloss of 'moment.'
usageInScripture: This Greek noun appears only once in the New Testament, where it is translated as 'a moment' in Luke 4:5. The consistency of this translation aligns with its broader lexical range, which includes references to a point in time or a brief instant. The singular occurrence in Scripture emphasizes its use to denote an extremely brief, sharply defined period, underscoring the fleeting nature of time in that context. This focused usage highlights the word’s precision and immediacy.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding στιγμή as a sharply defined moment enriches our grasp of biblical temporality and divine sovereignty over time. It reminds believers that God’s purposes and actions can unfold within even the briefest of instants, underscoring His control over all moments. This insight invites faith in the immediacy and power of God’s intervention in history and personal life. Moreover, the root idea of a 'mark' or 'brand' suggests that moments in time are not random but carry significance and divine imprint, encouraging believers to live with awareness of God's purposeful design in every instant.
keyVerseReflection: In Luke 4:5, the devil shows Jesus all the kingdoms of the world 'in a moment of time,' using στιγμή to emphasize the swift and comprehensive nature of this vision. The word highlights how quickly the devil’s temptation unfolds, compressing the vast scope of the world’s kingdoms into a single, sharp instant. This underscores the immediacy of the spiritual testing Jesus faces and the transient nature of worldly power compared to eternal kingdom realities.
